client.name: Fernhill Market
client.description: A 22-store regional grocery chain with a loyal but ageing customer base, under price pressure from discount chains.

engagement.goal: Decide whether a loyalty app is the right investment to grow repeat visits, and if so, what it should do first.
constraints: Capital budget for digital is fixed at £400k this year
Point-of-sale system is 9 years old; vendor support ends in 18 months

items.source: In-store intercept survey, 410 shoppers across 6 stores
items.summary: 58% said they would 'probably' or 'definitely' use a Fernhill loyalty app if it offered personalised discounts.

items.source: Existing paper/keytag loyalty scheme data, 3 years
items.summary: Only 14% of active keytag members redeemed a reward in the last 12 months, and keytag sign-ups have declined 9% year on year.

items.source: Till transaction data, all stores, 12 months
items.summary: Customers aged 60+ account for 46% of revenue. Average basket size is stable; visit frequency has fallen 6% year on year.
Most cited price as the reason they shop elsewhere more often. Three mentioned long queues at peak times. None mentioned the lack of an app.
Commercial director believes the main reason for falling visits is the lack of a digital offer, citing competitors' apps.
Store managers report peak-time queues of 10+ minutes at 4 of 5 stores interviewed, driven by understaffed tills rather than till hardware.
The current POS cannot accept app-based digital coupons without a middleware layer. Vendor estimate: 4–6 months and £150–220k.

items.source: Review of 4 competitor apps and public app-store data
items.summary: Two discount competitors have apps with 4.5+ ratings; the two regional competitors' apps have under 10k downloads each and ratings below 3.
Among shoppers aged 60+, 31% said they would use an app; 52% said they would prefer offers printed on receipts or mailed.
Personalised coupons printed on receipts were redeemed at 11% vs 3% for generic coupons (n≈18,000 receipts). Early, two stores only.
A board member said 'everyone under 40 expects an app now'.
